records.explicit_detail: Matthew says Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to John to be baptized.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Mark names Nazareth; Matthew 3:13 does not.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew alone in this set records John's initial objection and Jesus' reply about fulfilling all righteousness.
records.speaker: John the Baptist / Jesus
records.sequence_boundary: Do not attribute this exchange to Mark, Luke, or John.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew reports the Spirit of God descending like a dove after Jesus' baptism.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: The wording and viewpoint of the heavenly voice differ among witnesses.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew orders the temptations as stones to bread, temple pinnacle, then kingdoms of the world.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Luke presents the second and third temptations in the reverse order.

records.explicit_detail: Mark identifies Jesus as coming from Nazareth of Galilee and being baptized by John in the Jordan.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew says from Galilee but does not name Nazareth in this baptism scene.

records.explicit_detail: Mark says the heavens were torn open and the Spirit descended on Jesus like a dove.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not replace Mark's wording with Matthew's 'opened' formulation.

records.explicit_detail: Mark says the Spirit immediately drove Jesus into the wilderness.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew and Luke use different verbs for the Spirit-led transition.

records.explicit_detail: Mark alone among these temptation narratives explicitly says Jesus was with the wild animals while angels served him.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import the three detailed temptation dialogues from Matthew or Luke into Mark.

records.explicit_detail: Luke places Jesus' baptism in the setting 'when all the people were baptized' and says Jesus was praying.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew and Mark do not state Jesus was praying at the baptism.

records.explicit_detail: Luke describes the Holy Spirit descending in bodily form like a dove.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not flatten Luke's 'bodily form' into every witness.

records.explicit_detail: Luke says Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, was led by the Spirit in the wilderness for forty days.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Mark says the Spirit drove him; preserve each witness's wording.

records.explicit_detail: Luke orders the temptations as stone to bread, kingdoms, then Jerusalem/temple pinnacle.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew orders the kingdoms after the temple-pinnacle temptation.

records.explicit_detail: John's Gospel has John the Baptist testify that he saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove and remaining on Jesus.
records.speaker: John the Baptist
records.sequence_boundary: John 1:29–34 does not narrate the baptism act itself.

records.explicit_detail: The Baptist says the one who sent him to baptize in water had given him the identifying sign about the Spirit remaining.
records.speaker: John the Baptist
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import the Synoptic heavenly-voice wording into John 1:29–34.

records.explicit_detail: John 1:29–34 supplies retrospective witness testimony rather than a temptation narrative.
records.speaker: Narrator / John the Baptist
records.sequence_boundary: The temptation scene is not stated in this Johannine scope.

records.explicit_detail: The Baptist explicitly says he saw and testified; the passage grounds its claim in his reported observation.
records.speaker: John the Baptist
records.sequence_boundary: The exact title following 'testified that this is...' is textually variant and is not required by this node.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew places the call of Simon Peter and Andrew by the Sea of Galilee while they were casting a net.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Luke's call scene includes a miraculous catch; Matthew does not.

records.explicit_detail: Jesus tells Simon and Andrew to follow him and that he will make them fishers for people.
records.speaker: Jesus
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import Luke's 'do not be afraid' wording into Matthew.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew says Simon and Andrew immediately left their nets and followed Jesus.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew does not narrate a large catch before this response.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew says James and John left the boat and their father Zebedee after Jesus called them.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Mark additionally mentions hired servants; Matthew does not.

records.explicit_detail: Mark places Simon and Andrew casting a net in the Sea of Galilee when Jesus calls them.
records.speaker: Narrator / Jesus
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import Luke's boat-teaching and catch sequence.

records.explicit_detail: Mark says Simon and Andrew immediately left the nets and followed Jesus.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: The passage does not say they first brought boats to shore.

records.explicit_detail: Mark finds James and John in the boat mending nets with Zebedee nearby in the scene.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import Matthew's wording as though verbatim Mark.

records.explicit_detail: Mark uniquely in this pair says James and John left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired servants.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew 4:22 mentions the father and boat but not hired servants.

records.explicit_detail: Luke sets the scene at the lake of Gennesaret with two boats and Jesus teaching from Simon's boat.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew and Mark do not narrate boat teaching in their call scene.

records.explicit_detail: At Jesus' instruction Simon lets down the nets and the catch becomes so large that the nets begin to break.
records.speaker: Jesus / Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import this catch into Matthew 4 or Mark 1.

records.explicit_detail: Simon Peter falls at Jesus' knees and calls himself a sinful man.
records.speaker: Simon Peter
records.sequence_boundary: This self-description is not stated in Matthew 4 or Mark 1.

records.explicit_detail: Luke says James and John are Simon's partners and that after bringing the boats to land they left everything and followed Jesus.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew/Mark present a different local sequence.

records.explicit_detail: John says two of John the Baptist's disciples followed Jesus after hearing the Baptist identify him.
records.speaker: John the Baptist / Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not equate this scene with the Sea of Galilee fishermen call.

records.explicit_detail: Andrew is identified as one of the two and tells Simon that they have found the Messiah before bringing him to Jesus.
records.speaker: Narrator / Andrew
records.sequence_boundary: The other of the two disciples is not named in this passage.

records.explicit_detail: Jesus finds Philip and says 'Follow me'; Philip is said to be from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.
records.speaker: Jesus / Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import the fishing-net setting into this Johannine scene.

records.explicit_detail: Philip finds Nathanael; Nathanael questions whether anything good can come from Nazareth, and Philip invites him to come and see.
records.speaker: Philip / Nathanael
records.sequence_boundary: Nathanael is not part of the Matthew 4/Mark 1 fishermen-call wording.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew says Jesus came to his own city and a paralytic lying on a bed was brought to him.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Mark explicitly names Capernaum; Matthew 9:1–8 does not.

records.explicit_detail: Jesus sees their faith and tells the paralytic that his sins are forgiven.
records.speaker: Jesus
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew does not describe four carriers or a roof opening.

records.explicit_detail: Some scribes say to themselves that Jesus is blaspheming, and Jesus addresses their thoughts.
records.speaker: scribes / Jesus
records.sequence_boundary: Mark gives a fuller internal-reasoning formulation.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew ends with the crowds marveling and glorifying God who had given such authority to men.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not replace Matthew's closing reaction with Mark's 'we never saw anything like this'.

records.explicit_detail: Mark explicitly locates the scene in Capernaum after some days, with a crowd filling the house and doorway.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew calls it Jesus' own city but does not narrate the crowded doorway.

records.explicit_detail: Four people carry the paralytic and open the roof because they cannot get through the crowd.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew does not state the number four or the roof action.

records.explicit_detail: The scribes reason in their hearts that only God can forgive sins; Jesus perceives their reasoning.
records.speaker: scribes / Jesus
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import Luke's named Pharisees and teachers-of-law gathering.

records.explicit_detail: The healed man immediately takes up his mat and goes out before everyone; the people say they never saw anything like it.
records.speaker: Narrator / crowd
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew's crowd response is worded differently.

records.explicit_detail: Luke introduces Pharisees and teachers of the law from Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem sitting while Jesus teaches.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Mark names Capernaum but Luke 5:17 does not in this scene.

records.explicit_detail: Men carry a paralyzed man on a bed and lower him through the roof tiles into the middle before Jesus.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Luke does not state the number of carriers here.

records.explicit_detail: Jesus calls the man 'Man' and says his sins are forgiven; scribes and Pharisees question who can forgive sins but God alone.
records.speaker: Jesus / scribes and Pharisees
records.sequence_boundary: Mark addresses the paralytic as 'Son'; preserve witness wording.

records.explicit_detail: Luke closes with amazement, glorifying God, fear, and the statement that they had seen strange things that day.
records.speaker: Narrator / crowd
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import Mark's exact closing acclamation.

records.explicit_detail: John 5 describes a different healing in Jerusalem by a pool with five covered porches; it is not the Synoptic roof-paralytic scene.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not harmonize John 5 with Matthew 9, Mark 2, or Luke 5.

records.explicit_detail: John's healed man says he has no one to put him into the pool when the water is stirred.
records.speaker: healed man
records.sequence_boundary: The Synoptic paralytic narratives do not contain this pool explanation.

records.explicit_detail: Jesus tells the man to arise, take up his mat, and walk; the man is immediately made well.
records.speaker: Jesus / Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Similarity of mat-language does not prove identity of events.

records.explicit_detail: John foregrounds a Sabbath controversy because the healed man carries his mat on the Sabbath.
records.speaker: Narrator / opponents
records.sequence_boundary: The Synoptic roof-paralytic scene in the assigned passages is not framed as a Sabbath controversy.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew introduces an unnamed ruler who says his daughter has just died and asks Jesus to lay a hand on her.
records.speaker: ruler
records.sequence_boundary: Mark and Luke name the ruler Jairus and initially describe the girl as dying.

records.explicit_detail: The woman has had a discharge of blood for twelve years and touches the fringe of Jesus' garment.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew does not narrate physicians or expense.

records.explicit_detail: Jesus turns, sees the woman, and tells her to take heart because her faith has made her well.
records.speaker: Jesus
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew does not include a 'Who touched me?' exchange.

records.explicit_detail: At the ruler's house Matthew mentions flute players and a noisy crowd before Jesus takes the girl by the hand and she rises.
records.speaker: Narrator / Jesus
records.sequence_boundary: Mark and Luke include other details not stated by Matthew.

records.explicit_detail: Mark names Jairus as a synagogue ruler and says his little daughter is at the point of death when he appeals to Jesus.
records.speaker: Narrator / Jairus
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew does not name Jairus in its parallel.

records.explicit_detail: Mark says the woman suffered under many physicians, spent all she had, and became worse before touching Jesus' clothing.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew and Luke do not include this full physician/expense description.

records.explicit_detail: Jesus perceives that power has gone out from him and asks who touched his clothes; the woman comes fearing and trembling and tells the truth.
records.speaker: Jesus / Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew does not narrate this inquiry.

records.explicit_detail: Mark records the Aramaic 'Talitha cumi', says the girl was twelve, and notes she rose and walked; Jesus orders food for her.
records.speaker: Jesus / Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import Mark's Aramaic wording into Matthew or Luke.

records.explicit_detail: Luke names Jairus, identifies him as a synagogue ruler, and says he had an only daughter about twelve years old who was dying.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Mark says little daughter near death; Luke uniquely says only daughter in this scope.

records.explicit_detail: Luke says the woman had a twelve-year discharge of blood and could not be healed by anyone.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import Mark's physician/expense wording into Luke.

records.explicit_detail: When Jesus asks who touched him, Peter notes that the crowds surround and press him; Jesus says he knows power went out from him.
records.speaker: Jesus / Peter
records.sequence_boundary: Mark's disciples respond collectively; Luke names Peter.

records.explicit_detail: Luke says the girl's spirit returned; she rose immediately, and Jesus directed that she be given something to eat.
records.speaker: Narrator / Jesus
records.sequence_boundary: Mark says she rose and walked; Luke explicitly says her spirit returned.

records.explicit_detail: John 4 narrates a different healing involving a royal official's son who was sick at Capernaum while Jesus was in Cana.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not identify this official with Jairus.

records.explicit_detail: The official asks Jesus to come down and heal his son before the child dies.
records.speaker: royal official
records.sequence_boundary: This is not the Jairus wording or house sequence.

records.explicit_detail: Jesus tells the official that his son lives, and the man believes the word and goes his way.
records.speaker: Jesus / Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: The Synoptic Jairus scenes narrate Jesus going to the house.

records.explicit_detail: The servants meet the official and report that the child lives; the father learns the fever left at the hour Jesus spoke.
records.speaker: servants / Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: This confirmation sequence is unique to this Johannine healing.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew says Jesus withdrew by boat to a deserted place, and the crowds followed on foot from the cities.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import John's mountain setting or Mark's green-grass grouping into Matthew.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew says Jesus had compassion on the great multitude and healed their sick.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Mark emphasizes teaching because they were like sheep without a shepherd; preserve Matthew's stated emphasis.

records.explicit_detail: When the disciples proposed sending the crowds away, Jesus told them they did not need to go away and said, 'You give them something to eat.'
records.speaker: disciples / Jesus
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew reports five loaves and two fish, about five thousand men besides women and children, and twelve baskets of leftovers.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew explicitly adds 'besides women and children'; do not attribute that wording to every witness.

records.explicit_detail: Mark opens with the apostles gathering to Jesus and reporting what they had done and taught.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Mark says Jesus had compassion because the crowd was like sheep without a shepherd, and he began to teach them many things.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not replace Mark's teaching emphasis with Matthew's healing statement.

records.explicit_detail: Mark alone in this assigned comparison specifies that the people sat on the green grass in groups by hundreds and fifties.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Mark reports five loaves and two fish, five thousand men, and twelve baskets full of broken pieces and fish.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Luke says the apostles returned and told Jesus what they had done, after which he withdrew with them toward a city called Bethsaida.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not silently replace Luke's Bethsaida wording with another Gospel's destination.

records.explicit_detail: Luke says Jesus welcomed the crowds, spoke to them about the Kingdom of God, and healed those who needed healing.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Luke records Jesus telling the disciples to make the people sit in groups of about fifty each.
records.speaker: Jesus
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Luke reports five loaves and two fish, about five thousand men, and twelve baskets of broken pieces left over.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: John says Jesus asked Philip where bread could be bought for the crowd, adding that Jesus said this to test him.
records.speaker: Jesus / narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Andrew identifies a boy who has five barley loaves and two fish.
records.speaker: Andrew
records.sequence_boundary: The boy and barley specification belong to John's account in this comparison.

records.explicit_detail: John notes there was much grass in the place and that about five thousand men sat down.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: After the sign, John says the people identified Jesus as the prophet who comes into the world, and Jesus withdrew to the mountain when he perceived they intended to make him king by force.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew says Jesus immediately made the disciples enter the boat and go ahead while he dismissed the crowds.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: After dismissing the crowds, Matthew says Jesus went up the mountain alone to pray while the boat was being battered by the waves.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew records the disciples crying out in fear that they saw a ghost, and Jesus answering them to take courage and not be afraid.
records.speaker: disciples / Jesus
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew uniquely in this comparison narrates Peter leaving the boat, walking toward Jesus, sinking when afraid, being rescued, and the boat's occupants worshiping Jesus.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Mark says Jesus made the disciples get into the boat and go ahead toward Bethsaida while he sent the multitude away.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: John describes the disciples as going toward Capernaum; do not erase the witness-specific destination wording.

records.explicit_detail: Mark says Jesus saw the disciples distressed in rowing because the wind was contrary.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Mark states that Jesus came to them walking on the sea and 'would have passed by them' before they cried out.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: The phrase about passing by is Mark's wording in this assigned comparison.

records.explicit_detail: After Jesus entered the boat and the wind ceased, Mark says the disciples were greatly amazed because they had not understood about the loaves and their hearts were hardened.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Luke's feeding account ends with the crowd eating, being filled, and twelve baskets of leftovers being gathered.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: This cited Luke scope does not continue into a walking-on-water narrative.

records.explicit_detail: The cited Luke passage does not state that Jesus sent the disciples across the lake immediately after the feeding.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: 'Not stated in the cited text' is the correct source-scope conclusion.

records.explicit_detail: The cited Luke passage does not narrate Jesus walking on the sea.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import Matthew/Mark/John's sea scene into Luke.

records.explicit_detail: The cited Luke passage does not narrate Peter walking on the water.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Peter's water-walking episode is Matthew-specific in this assigned corpus.

records.explicit_detail: John says the disciples went down to the sea after evening came and entered a boat to go across toward Capernaum; Jesus had not yet come to them.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: John says the sea was rising because a great wind was blowing.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: After rowing about twenty-five or thirty stadia, the disciples saw Jesus walking on the sea and drawing near the boat, and they were afraid.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: John says the disciples were willing to receive Jesus into the boat, and immediately the boat was at the land where they were going.
records.speaker: Jesus / narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew locates Jesus' question about his identity in the region of Caesarea Philippi.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew records Simon Peter answering that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God, followed by Jesus blessing Simon and attributing the disclosure to the Father.
records.speaker: Peter / Jesus
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew says that after six days Jesus took Peter, James, and John up a high mountain by themselves and was transfigured before them.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew describes a bright cloud overshadowing them and a voice identifying Jesus as the beloved Son and commanding the disciples to listen to him.
records.speaker: voice from cloud
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Mark says Jesus and his disciples went into the villages of Caesarea Philippi when he asked who people and the disciples said he was.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Mark records Peter answering, 'You are the Christ.'
records.speaker: Peter
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import Matthew's longer confession wording into Mark.

records.explicit_detail: Mark says that after six days Jesus took Peter, James, and John up a high mountain and was transfigured before them.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Mark emphasizes that Jesus' clothing became exceedingly white and records Peter's fear as he proposed making three tents.
records.speaker: narrator / Peter
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Luke introduces the identity question while Jesus was praying alone and the disciples were with him.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.place: not named in the cited verse
records.sequence_boundary: Luke does not name Caesarea Philippi in this scene.

records.explicit_detail: Luke records Peter answering, 'The Christ of God.'
records.speaker: Peter
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Luke says that about eight days after these sayings Jesus took Peter, John, and James and went up the mountain to pray.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Matthew and Mark say after six days; preserve Luke's 'about eight days' wording.

records.explicit_detail: Luke states that Moses and Elijah appeared in glory and spoke about Jesus' departure/exodus that he was about to accomplish at Jerusalem.
records.speaker: Moses and Elijah
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: John 12 places Jesus speaking about his troubled soul and the coming hour in a Jerusalem festival context rather than a mountain transfiguration scene.
records.speaker: Jesus
records.sequence_boundary: Do not identify John 12 as John's version of the Transfiguration.

records.explicit_detail: A voice from heaven answers Jesus' prayer to glorify the Father's name, saying it has been glorified and will be glorified again.
records.speaker: voice from heaven
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: John says the crowd standing there interpreted the sound differently: some said it thundered and others that an angel spoke to Jesus.
records.speaker: crowd
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Jesus says the voice came not for his sake but for the crowd's sake, then speaks of judgment and being lifted up.
records.speaker: Jesus
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew says Jesus sent two disciples from Bethphage at the Mount of Olives to find a donkey tied with a colt beside her.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not flatten Matthew's donkey-and-colt wording into the other witnesses.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew explicitly connects the animal scene with prophetic fulfillment wording about the king coming humble and riding on a donkey and colt.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew records crowds crying 'Hosanna to the son of David' and blessing the one coming in the Lord's name.
records.speaker: crowds
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Matthew says the whole city was stirred and asked, 'Who is this?' and the crowds answered that this was the prophet Jesus from Nazareth of Galilee.
records.speaker: city / crowds
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Mark says Jesus sent two disciples near Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives to find a colt on which no one had sat.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Mark includes an exchange with bystanders who ask why the disciples are untying the colt; the disciples answer as Jesus instructed.
records.speaker: bystanders / disciples
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Mark records acclamations including blessing for the coming kingdom of their father David.
records.speaker: crowd
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Mark says Jesus entered Jerusalem and the temple, looked around at everything, and because it was already late went out to Bethany with the Twelve.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: This look-around-and-depart sequence is distinctive to Mark's local narrative.

records.explicit_detail: Luke says Jesus sent two disciples near Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives to find a colt on which no one had ever sat.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Luke records the colt's owners asking why it was being untied; the disciples answer that the Lord needs it.
records.speaker: owners / disciples
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Luke has the multitude of disciples praise God for the mighty works they had seen and acclaim the king who comes in the Lord's name.
records.speaker: multitude of disciples
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: Luke alone in this assigned entry comparison narrates Jesus weeping over Jerusalem and speaking about its failure to know the things that make for peace and the time of visitation.
records.speaker: Jesus
records.sequence_boundary: Do not import parallel-witness details not stated in this cited scope.

records.explicit_detail: John explicitly says the crowd took branches of palm trees and went out to meet Jesus.
records.speaker: Narrator
records.sequence_boundary: Palm branches are explicitly stated by John in this comparison; do not assume each witness uses the same detail.

records.explicit_detail: John records the crowd acclaiming the King of Israel in addition to the blessing for the one coming in the Lord's name.
